=== Manual testing

- Fixed an issue where *Set device timezone* failed on iOS simulators in manual sessions and showed `Cannot set the device time zone. Please try again.` You can now change the time zone of an iOS simulator from the session toolbar, and the simulator's status bar clock shows the new time zone.
- Each time zone change on an iOS simulator pauses the simulator screen for several seconds and closes the app in the foreground. Relaunch the app to continue testing.
- When the cleanup policy resets the time zone after a session, iOS simulators now return to the time zone of their host.

=== Kobiton CLI

* *iOS simulators:* `kobiton file list`, `kobiton file push`, `kobiton file pull`, and `kobiton device ps` now work on iOS simulators. Previously, `file list`, `file pull`, and `device ps` failed with a server error, and `file push` reported success without writing the file. The CLI now refuses paths outside the app's container on simulators.
* *iOS devices and simulators:* `kobiton file push` now fails with a non-zero exit code when the target app is not installed or not accessible. Previously, the push printed `Pushed <n> bytes` and exited `0` even though no file was written.

// Source: KOB-55419 from PR #753
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/753

=== Manual testing

- Fixed an issue where app installation errors in manual sessions hid the error reported by the device. For some iOS and Android errors, Kobiton Portal replaced the device error with its own explanation, which could point to the wrong cause. The error message now shows the device error text after `Failed to install '<app>'.`, for example `ApplicationVerificationFailed`, `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE`, `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`, `INSTALL_FAILED_OLDER_SDK`, or `DeviceOSVersionTooLow`. When an install error includes a Kobiton error code, the code still appears at the start of the message.
- iOS installs that fail signature verification now show the `ApplicationVerificationFailed` error instead of an AS-500 message stating that *App signing using Kobiton Certificate (iOS)* is disabled. This error means the app's own signature isn't valid on the device, for example, because the provisioning profile doesn't include the device UDID or the profile or certificate has expired.

=== App management

* *iOS Simulator builds:* The app repository now accepts iOS Simulator builds (`.app` bundles). Compress the `.app` bundle to a `.zip` file, then upload it from the app repository, API v2, or the Kobiton CLI. A `.app` file that is a `.zip` archive is also accepted. Selecting an uncompressed `.app` in the app repository displays a message to compress it first.
* *Simulator apps in the app repository:* Simulator apps display the Apple watermark and support search, versions, lock, delete, and download, the same as other iOS apps. Simulator builds can't be installed on real devices. For details, see xref:apps:supported-filetypes.adoc[].

// Source: KOB-55176 from PR #748
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/748

== Install Apps lists only compatible builds on iOS

*Install Apps* in a manual session now lists only the app builds that can install on the current iOS device.

*Highlights*

- On an iOS Simulator, only simulator builds (`.app`) are listed. On a real iOS device, simulator builds are hidden.
- *Upload File* and *Install From URL* accept a `.app` compressed to a `.zip` file on iOS Simulators.
- Android sessions are unchanged.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:install-an-app.adoc#_apps_listed_on_ios[Apps listed on iOS].

== Fixed device release in earlier virtualUSB versions

- Fixed an issue where virtualUSB versions earlier than 4.20.0 failed to release a connected device. Running `vusb disconnect --udid <device-udid>`, or stopping `vusb connect` with Ctrl+C, reported `Device access ticket is not found`, and the virtualUSB session kept running in Kobiton Portal until it was terminated there. These commands now end the virtualUSB session and release the device, whether it was connected from the CLI or the virtualUSB app. No virtualUSB update is required.

=== Standalone deployment

- On Standalone deployments with GPUs, Intelligent Quality Suite (IQS) AI services now keep GPU access after system package installs, such as a GigaCap install or upgrade. Previously, these services could switch to the CPU, and IQS element finding slowed down and timed out.
- Installing or updating Standalone now stops with an error if a configured GPU ID does not match a GPU on the host. Previously, the install continued without reporting the problem.
- After you update, the IQS AI services restart once to apply the new GPU configuration.

// Source: KOB-55464 from PR #746
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/746

== iOS location permission alert in XIUM sessions

- Fixed an issue where, on iOS 26, scripts could not find the buttons on the location permission alert, such as *Allow Once*, *Allow While Using App*, and *Don't Allow*. The page source now includes the alert and its buttons, so scripts can locate them and accept or dismiss the alert. Previously, the page source sometimes showed only the map inside the alert, and scripts failed with a `no such element` error.

// Source: KOB-55504 from PR #735
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/735

== Fewer duplicate steps in Kobiton CLI session timelines

The Session Explorer timeline for Kobiton CLI sessions no longer shows an extra `POST /session` step for every `kobiton webdriver` call. The timeline now shows the session creation once, followed by one step for each call.

* Repeated session creation requests are hidden from the timeline but remain in the session's command data.
* A failed session creation request still appears as a step.
* The device logs for each call include the log lines since the previous call.
* CLI sessions recorded before this change display the same way.

Automation and mixed sessions are not affected.

AI assistants can tell when results are truncated and narrow the search by platform, device name, UDID, or device group. == Scan completeness in the Kobiton MCP server

AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server can now tell whether a session's validation scans have finished. Previously, a scan that was still running could return the same empty result as a finished scan with no findings.

- `getSession` returns a `scan_status` block with an entry for accessibility, crash, response time, and Flex Correct scans. Each entry is `complete`, `in_progress`, or `not_applicable`.
- `getAccessibilityValidationsSummary` returns a `scan_complete` flag that matches the accessibility entry in `scan_status`.
- `listCrashValidations` returns a `pending_count` of crash logs that are still being processed, so an in-progress crash is no longer reported as no crash.
- `getTestRun` returns `accessibility_scanning_status`, `crash_scanning_status`, and `network_payload_scanning_status` on each execution.
- The validation tool descriptions now tell the assistant that results may be partial while scanning runs and to check `scan_status` before treating a result as final.

== Leaner screen reads in the Kobiton automate plugin

The `drive-automation-session` and `run-interactive-session` skills now give your AI assistant a filtered view of the screen's UI tree by default. The filtered view keeps only interactive and labeled elements, such as elements with an ID, accessibility label, or text, or elements that are clickable, along with their bounds. This reduces how much of the page source your AI assistant reads on each step of a session.

- Filtering now applies to native Android and iOS screens as well as webviews.
- The full page source and screenshot are still captured, and your AI assistant can read them when the filtered view isn't enough.

Requires Kobiton automate plugin version 1.15.0 or later.

// Source: KOB-55267 from PR #719
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/719

=== Kobiton MCP server

* `listTestCases`, `listTestSuites`, and `listTestRuns` now return at most 20 items per call. `rowsPerPage` defaults to 10 and is clamped to the range 1 to 20, and `total_items` still reports the full count so an assistant can page through larger result sets. This keeps an AI assistant from requesting a response too large for its context.
* `getUserInputEvents` now returns at most 20 events per call. `limit` defaults to 10, down from 50, and is clamped to the range 1 to 20.
* The four tool descriptions now state the default and maximum page size.

These limits apply to the MCP tools only. The REST API and Kobiton Portal are unchanged.

== Fold and unfold foldable devices in manual sessions

Manual sessions on foldable Android devices, such as Galaxy Z Fold and Pixel Fold, now include a fold control in the session toolbar.

* The control appears above *Rotate Screen* on foldable devices and shows the action it performs next: *Fold device* or *Unfold device*.
* The session starts in the device's physical posture.
* After a fold or unfold, the device screen and *Inspector* switch to the size and shape of the active screen.
* Folds and unfolds are recorded as steps in Session Explorer.

Flip-style foldable devices, such as Galaxy Z Flip, are not supported.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:device-controls.adoc#_fold_or_unfold_device[Device controls].

== deviceConnect Console

- The device list and the device details page now show how many errors each device had in the last hour, for example *3 errors in the last hour*. - When a device has more than 10 errors in the last hour, the error count turns orange and links to troubleshooting guidance for offline devices. The warning clears when the hourly count drops to 10 or fewer.

== Reset stuck device states with the Kobiton API

Org admins can now use the Kobiton API to reset devices whose state is stuck on the wrong value, such as a device that still shows as in use after its session has ended. Stuck devices no longer require a manual database change to return to service.

The new `POST /v2/execute-admin-tasks` endpoint runs predefined admin tasks. The first available task, `RESET_DEVICE_STATE`, accepts a list of device UDIDs and resets the state of each device to the default state.

* Returns the previous state and new state for each device, plus a summary of how many devices were reset, unchanged, or failed.
* Processes each device independently. If one device fails, the other devices in the request are still processed.
* Changes only the device state recorded in Kobiton. The task does not send commands to the device or its host machine, and it does not end sessions or cancel reservations.
* Limits org admins to devices in their own organization. Available for Cloud and Standalone.

After a reset, the device becomes available for sessions the next time its host machine reports on the device.

== List the apps installed on a device with the API

* New API endpoints return the apps installed on a private device, including apps installed outside your app repository, such as through MDM or manually:
** `+GET /v2/devices/{deviceId}/installed-apps+`
** `+GET /v2/devices/udid/{udid}/installed-apps+`
* Each app in the response includes its bundle ID, name, version, and build version. On Android devices, the app name is empty.
* To include the app repository version ID for apps that match a version in your app repository, add `includeKobitonAppVersionId=true` to the request.
* The `type` parameter accepts `user`, `system`, `all`, `filesharing`, `enabled`, and `disabled`. Currently, the endpoints return every app on the device, including system apps, and the `type_applied` response field reports the filter that was applied.
* If the device is offline or does not respond, the endpoints return an error that describes the problem.
* `+GET /v2/devices/{deviceId}/apps+` is unchanged and continues to return only apps that are in your app repository.

== Scan status and page limits in the Kobiton MCP server

- `getSession` now returns `scan_status`, which reports whether each validation scan for the session is `complete`, `in_progress`, or `not_applicable`. An AI assistant can tell findings that are still arriving from final results.
- `getAccessibilityValidationsSummary` now returns `scan_complete`, and `listCrashValidations` now returns `pending_count`, the number of crash logs still waiting to be processed.
- `getTestRun` and `listTestRuns` now return the accessibility, crash, and network payload scanning status of each execution.
- `listTestCases`, `listTestSuites`, and `listTestRuns` return at most 20 items per page, with a default of 10. `getUserInputEvents` now returns 10 events by default and at most 20 per call.
- `listDevices` now reports how many devices matched in total for each device list, along with the `limit` it applied.
- In the `automate` plugin 1.15.0, the `drive-automation-session` and `run-interactive-session` skills read a compact UI tree of the screen by default. The full page source is still available on request.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc[Kobiton AI plugin and tools reference].

=== Organization settings for Appium AI

Administrators can now configure Appium AI for the whole organization in Kobiton Portal. New Appium sessions use the organization's LLM provider and locator settings without requiring per-session configuration.

*Highlights*

* Turn Appium AI on or off for the organization.
* Set the default LLM endpoint, API key, API format, text and vision models, extra request body, locator strategy, and coordinate space.
* Require an API key whenever an LLM endpoint is set, except for the Ollama chat API format.
* Apply saved settings to new sessions on every device host in the organization. Running sessions keep their current settings.
* Override organization settings for a single session with `kobiton:*` desired capabilities.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

=== Appium AI organization settings

Organizations can now turn Appium AI on or off and set a default LLM provider in Kobiton. Appium sessions started by members of the organization use these settings, so LLM provider details no longer need to be entered in `dc.ini` on each host.

* Turn Appium AI on or off for the whole organization.
* Set a default LLM provider base URL, API key, API format, models, and locator strategy.
* Override any provider setting for a single session with `kobiton:*` capabilities.
* Existing `dc.ini` configurations continue to work.

Appium AI remains in Beta and is not available for Public Cloud devices.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-for-your-organization.adoc[Configure Appium AI for your organization].

== Passcode entry in iOS manual sessions

Enter the device passcode on the iOS system passcode screen during a manual session. This screen appears for Apple Pay, the Wallet *Add Card* flow, and the hidden apps folder, and iOS hides its keypad from the session video stream.

* A numeric keypad overlay appears on the session stream when the passcode screen is detected. Tap the overlay to enter the passcode.
* Select *Auto-fill passcode* to enter the device's configured passcode.
* Use the *Passcode helper* menu on the session toolbar to show or hide the keypad overlay and to auto-fill the passcode.

== Passcode support on the Devices page

* Filter the device list by *Passcode*, with *Supported* or *Not Supported* values, in the device search bar.
* A passcode icon next to the device name in card view and list view marks devices ready for passcode entry. Hover over the icon to show *Passcode enabled - required for Apple Pay*.

A device is supported when your organization has passcode (PIN) mode enabled and the device has a passcode set.

== Apple Pay passcode entry in manual sessions

Enter the device passcode on the Apple Pay confirmation screen during manual sessions on iOS devices. iOS displays this screen as blank in the live stream.

*Highlights*

* Click *Passcode helper* to show the hidden passcode keypad as a tappable overlay on the device screen.
* Taps on the overlay enter the passcode directly on the device. Entry progress shows as dots, and the digits are never displayed.
* The passcode helper supports iPhone screen sizes, portrait and landscape orientation, and Display Zoom.

*Availability*

Available in manual sessions only.

For steps, see xref:manual-testing:local-devices/use-apple-pay-in-manual-session.adoc[Use Apple Pay on iOS devices].

=== Cleanup on iOS Simulators

Cleanup now erases an iOS Simulator and returns it to its default state, instead of running the individual cleanup configurations.

*Highlights*

- Apps installed during the session, app data, Safari history and tabs, and Settings changes are removed when cleanup runs.
- The erase runs every time cleanup runs on a simulator, on any iOS version. The individual configurations in a cleanup policy don't apply to simulators. The _No Cleanup_ policy still skips cleanup.
- Time zone and locale return to the simulator's defaults.
- The simulator becomes available again without action on the host. Real iOS devices keep the cleanup configured in their policy.

For details, see xref:devices:local-devices/cleanup-policy/cleanup-configurations.adoc#_ios_simulators[iOS Simulators].

=== Appium automation

- On iOS Simulators, `mobile: queryAppState` and `mobile: isAppInstalled` now return the app state and installed status. Previously, both commands failed with a server error for every bundle ID, so scripts that waited for an app to reach the foreground, or checked whether an app was installed before installing it, stopped on simulators. Both commands now return the same values as on a real iOS device, including after `mobile: activateApp` and `mobile: terminateApp`.

=== Appium automation fixes

* Fixed an issue where requesting an attribute that an element doesn't have, such as `value`, returned an error in Android native app sessions. The WebDriver Get Element Attribute command now returns `null` for an absent attribute, as the W3C WebDriver specification requires, and the session remains usable. Known attributes such as `text`, `enabled`, and `checked` still return their values, and requests for a stale element still return an error.

=== Appium AI

- Appium AI now uses the LLM settings configured for your organization. Natural language finds use your organization's endpoint, models, and API key without host configuration changes or extra capabilities in test scripts. Session capabilities (`kobiton:llm*`) still take precedence, field by field. Organizations without LLM settings keep using the host defaults.
- Organization admins can turn off Appium AI for their organization. When Appium AI is off, natural language finds fail with the error `LLM client is disabled for this organization`, and session capabilities cannot turn it back on.
